high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Korean earth-pigment illustration of an onggijang building one breathing earthenware jar through repeated clay coils, stopping when the finished rim reaches a leaf-shaped completion gauge below a higher wooden ceiling, so the craft ends early when complete yet can never grow beyond its fixed bound.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A quiet Korean earthenware workshop has pale clay-plastered walls, exposed dark beams and a packed-earth floor scattered with small dry clay crumbs. Diffused daylight enters through one paper-latticed window. The scene uses soot-black ink, iron brown, persimmon orange, celadon grey and rice-paper cream in flattened hand-painted forms, with no photograph, writing, numeral, arrow, book, tablet, textile diagram, screen or ceremonial emblem.

elements.desc: Adult Korean onggijang seated at a low kick wheel, medium skin tone, black hair tied beneath a charcoal headcloth, muted indigo jacket, ochre trousers and clay-stained apron. Leaning forward with a calm concentrated expression, the potter has lowered the wooden paddle and open hands after completing the rim; no crown, badge, written plan, pointer, measuring tablet or modern machinery appears.

Onggi jar centered on the turning wheel, built from visible ascending clay coils blended into a continuous breathing vessel. Its rounded shoulder, narrow neck and finished lip remain below the upper crossbar, while a small pale leaf-shaped clay mark at the rim touches the lower completion feeler. No crack, duplicate vessel, inscription, number, label, screen or painted narrative panel appears.

Freestanding dark-wood gauge surrounding the jar without touching its body, formed by two vertical posts, one immovable upper crossbar and a lower pivoting feeler ending in a carved leaf shape. The completed rim lifts only the leaf feeler; the higher crossbar remains an absolute ceiling. The frame carries no scale marks, numerals, text, arrow, ruler plate or electronic sensor.

Remaining prepared clay resting at lower left as two thick curved coils and one compact kneaded block on a plain wooden board. The unused material stays separate because the jar has already satisfied its completion feeler before reaching the structural ceiling. It contains no written instruction, counted token, pottery shard label, arrow, glowing signal, decorative medallion or second unfinished jar.

Documented onggi tool set arranged on a low bench beside the jar: one patterned pine surae paddle, one rounded dogae anvil, one persimmon-wood smoothing blade and one folded damp finishing cloth. The tools remain separate from the explanatory gauge and carry no inscription, number, arrow, measuring scale, screen, decorative badge, electric motor or modern sensor.

Assistant standing near the unlit kiln entrance at right, medium skin tone, black hair in a low knot, rust-red jacket and dark trousers. Holding an empty wooden carrying ring at waist height, the assistant waits for the completed jar rather than adding another coil; the kiln remains closed and bears no lettering, royal ornament, sacred icon, clock or control panel.
